zero_omission_notes.summary: Chapter 1 covers the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, prime factorization, HCF and LCM calculations and their algebraic relation, and formal proofs of irrationality for square roots of prime numbers using proof by contradiction.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Every composite number can be expressed uniquely as a product of primes, up to the order of factors. For any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a,b) * LCM(a,b) = a * b.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Every composite number can be factorised as a product of primes uniquely.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Proof by contradiction: Assume √p is rational (p/q in lowest terms). Show p divides both p and q, contradicting coprime assumption.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Prime Divisibility
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Let p be a prime number. If p divides a^2, then p divides a, where a is a positive integer.

short_answer_questions.question: Prove that 3 + 2√5 is irrational.
short_answer_questions.answer: Assume 3 + 2√5 = a/b (rational). Then √5 = (a - 3b)/(2b). Left side is irrational while right side is rational, contradiction!

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Check whether 6^n can end with digit 0 for any natural number n.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: If 6^n ends in 0, 5 must be in its prime factorization. But 6^n = (2*3)^n = 2^n * 3^n. By uniqueness of FTA, 5 is not a factor. Hence 6^n never ends in 0.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Prove that √2 is irrational using proof by contradiction.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: Let √2 = a/b where a,b are coprime integers. 2 = a^2/b^2 => a^2 = 2b^2. Thus 2 divides a^2 => 2 divides a. Let a = 2c. Then 4c^2 = 2b^2 => b^2 = 2c^2 => 2 divides b. Thus 2 divides both a and b, contradicting that a and b are coprime. Hence √2 is irrational.

chapters.chapter_title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

zero_omission_notes.summary: Covers systems of two linear equations in two variables, graphical representation (intersecting, parallel, coincident lines), algebraic solutions (substitution, elimination), and consistency conditions based on coefficient ratios.

detailed_sections.full_explanation: a1 x + b1 y + c1 = 0 and a2 x + b2 y + c2 = 0. Intersecting (a1/a2 != b1/b2 -> unique solution), Coincident (a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 -> infinite solutions), Parallel (a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2 -> no solution).

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Ratio Conditions
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Unique: a1/a2 != b1/b2; Infinite: a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2; No solution: a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2

detailed_sections.full_explanation: Substitution: isolate one variable and substitute. Elimination: equalize coefficients of one variable by multiplication and add/subtract.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Elimination Choice

zero_omission_notes.summary: Covers second-degree equations ax^2 + bx + c = 0 (a != 0), standard form, solving by factorization and quadratic formula, and analyzing nature of roots via discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac.

detailed_sections.full_explanation: Quadratic equation standard form: ax^2 + bx + c = 0. Factorization splits middle term bx into two terms whose product is a*c.
Roots x = (-b ± √(b^2 - 4ac)) / (2a). Discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac: D > 0 (2 distinct real roots), D = 0 (2 equal real roots), D < 0 (no real roots).

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Find two consecutive odd positive integers whose sum of squares is 290.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: Let integers be x and x+2. x^2 + (x+2)^2 = 290 => 2x^2 + 4x + 4 = 290 => 2x^2 + 4x - 286 = 0 => x^2 + 2x - 143 = 0 => (x+13)(x-11) = 0. Since positive, x = 11. Integers are 11 and 13.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: A motorboat speed is 18 km/h in still water. Takes 1 hr more to go 24 km upstream than downstream. Find speed of stream.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: Let stream speed = x km/h. Upstream = 18-x, Downstream = 18+x. 24/(18-x) - 24/(18+x) = 1 => 24(18+x - 18+x)/(324 - x^2) = 1 => 48x = 324 - x^2 => x^2 + 48x - 324 = 0 => (x+54)(x-6) = 0. Speed cannot be negative => x = 6 km/h.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Diagonals of trapezium ABCD with AB || DC intersect at O. Show AO/BO = CO/DO.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: In ΔAOB and ΔCOD: ∠OAB = ∠OCD, ∠OBA = ∠ODC (alternate interior). ΔAOB ~ ΔCOD (AA) => AO/CO = BO/DO => AO/BO = CO/DO.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: If a line intersects sides AB and AC of ΔABC at D and E respectively and is parallel to BC, prove AD/AB = AE/AC.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: Since DE || BC, AD/DB = AE/EC by BPT. Taking reciprocals: DB/AD = EC/AE. Adding 1 to both sides: (DB+AD)/AD = (EC+AE)/AE => AB/AD = AC/AE. Inverting back: AD/AB = AE/AC.

1) sin^2 θ + cos^2 θ = 1; 2) 1 + tan^2 θ = sec^2 θ; 3) 1 + cot^2 θ = cosec^2 θ.

Substitute sin^2 θ = 1 - cos^2 θ = (1 - cos θ)(1 + cos θ)
LHS = (1 - cos θ) / (1 + cos θ) = RHS

zero_omission_notes.summary: Covers measures of central tendency for grouped data: Mean (Direct, Assumed Mean, Step-Deviation methods), Mode, Median, and empirical relation 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean.

detailed_sections.full_explanation: Direct: x̄ = Σfi xi / Σfi. Assumed Mean: x̄ = a + (Σfi di / Σfi). Step-Deviation: x̄ = a + [Σfi ui / Σfi] * h where ui = (xi - a)/h.

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 13.2 Mode and Median of Grouped Data
detailed_sections.full_explanation: Mode = l + [(f1 - f0)/(2f1 - f0 - f2)] * h. Median = l + [(n/2 - cf)/f] * h. Empirical formula: 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean.

zero_omission_notes.summary: Covers theoretical probability P(E) = n(E)/n(S), complementary events P(E) + P(Ē) = 1, impossible events (P=0), and certain events (P=1).

detailed_sections.full_explanation: For equally likely outcomes: P(E) = Number of favorable outcomes / Total possible outcomes. 0 <= P(E) <= 1.
Event 'not E' is Ē. P(E) + P(Ē) = 1. Impossible event P=0; Certain event P=1.
